newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Labor Dept to start issuing experimental CPI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Labor Dept to start issuing experimental CPI.

text.p: The Labor Department will soon begin publishing a new price index that takes into account consumers' tendencies to substitute similar products for one another in response to price changes, an economist with the department said Tuesday.
Patrick Jackman, an economist with the department's Bureau of Labor Statistics, said the agency will start issuing the new "geometric mean" index on an experimental basis sometime before April 15.
The index is an alternative to the government's official price gauge, the Consumer Price Index, which critics charge overstates inflation.

By taking into account the tendency of consumers' to substitute among similar products, such as purchasing Fuji apples when the price of McIntosh apples rises, the geometric mean index is expected to show slower increases than the CPI. However, the BLS said it does not have a firm estimate of the magnitude of the difference.

A congressionally appointed panel led by economist Michael Boskin recommended that the bureau officially adopt the geometric mean index as one way of dealing with a bias in the CPI, which the panel estimates at around 1.1 percentage points a year.

But BLS officials have said they want to study the geometric mean further before deciding whether to do so. Jackman said the bureau will decide by early next year whether to use the geometric metric in calculating all or part of the CPI. If it decides to use the new method, it would implement it starting in 1999.
Along with the issuance of the first geometric mean index, the bureau will publish six years of historical data comparing the changes in the experimental measure to those in the CPI.
